triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix match formula routed filing status 4 (surviving spouse / qualifying widow(er)) to the $250,000 joint-return threshold, but 26 USC 3101(b)(2)(A) grants that amount only "in the case of a joint return" and a surviving spouse falls under subparagraph (C), "in any other case, $200,000".
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/3101): (A) "in the case of a joint return, $250,000", (B) married filing separately = 1/2 of (A), (C) "in any other case, $200,000" — a surviving spouse does not file a joint return, so (C) controls; the diff matches exactly. Single-module commit; the only other module-file change is the module.summary prose, which was corrected in the same direction (status 1 narrowed from "joint / surviving spouse" to "joint", new line "4 = surviving spouse / qualifying widow(er)"), so nothing unrelated was touched. The companion test statutes/26/3101/b/2.test.yaml confirms the behavioral change (case renamed surviving_spouse_uses_joint_threshold -> surviving_spouse_uses_other_threshold; threshold 250000 -> 200000, excess 50000 -> 100000, tax 450 -> 900) and also drops four arithmetic comments, which is cosmetic. Kind could arguably be read as amount_mismatch since the effective threshold moved $250,000 -> $200,000, but the defect is which filing status the joint amount applied to, and the kind list names filing status explicitly under wrong_entity_or_scope; the parameter values themselves (250000 / 200000) were already correct and unchanged. Note on the quote: the PR body as stored on GitHub literally reads ",000" — the "$200" was lost when the PR was created (shell mangling), so the quote is verbatim but visibly truncated; PR title is "Repair 26 USC 3101(b)(2) surviving-spouse threshold". No reviews or review comments on PR #311. Commit body is empty apart from a newline.
triage.verifier_justification: The sole substantive change is the match arm routing filing status 4 (surviving spouse / qualifying widow(er)) from the $250,000 joint threshold to the $200,000 other-case threshold, with the companion test flipping 250000/50000/450 to 200000/100000/900; no parameter value, effective date, period, entity, or input/output changed. Read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-13, corpus commit 612d20ca43), 26 USC 3101(b)(2) grants $250,000 only "in the case of a joint return" (A) and $200,000 "in any other case" (C), and a surviving spouse does not file a joint return, so the pre-fix encoding disagreed with the source. I tried and failed to refute: it is not mechanical (a formula branch changed), not new coverage (the status-4 branch already existed pre-fix), and not amount_mismatch (both threshold parameters were already correct at 250000 and 200000 and were untouched — only the population routed to each changed). The closest competing kind is untraceable_branch (the arm was grounded on subparagraph (A) rather than (C)), but the branch itself is legitimate and the kind list enumerates "filing status" explicitly under wrong_entity_or_scope, so that remains the tighter fit.
